event.title: Around 2,200 Migrants Arrive in Canary Islands in Two Days
event.canonical_title: Around 2,200 Migrants Arrive in Canary Islands in Two Days
event.summary: Spain has reported that nearly 2,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands within a two-day period. This surge in arrivals, particularly from sub-Saharan Africa, prompted Spain to declare a migration emergency on November 11. The situation reflects a significant increase in migration attempts to the islands in recent weeks.

timeline.title: Record Number of Migrants Arrive in Canary Islands in One Day
timeline.summary: Nearly 2,000 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands in a single day, marking a record for the archipelago. The maritime rescue service reported that 1,990 individuals reached the islands aboard 15 boats, with many departing from Senegal and Gambia. This surge in arrivals coincides with Spain's upcoming elections, prompting concerns about unprecedented migration pressure on the region.

event_overview.title: About Migration Crisis
event_overview.subject: Migration Crisis
event_overview.summary: This event concerns maritime migration to Spain’s Canary Islands along the Western African Atlantic Route, which connects parts of West and North Africa with the Spanish archipelago. Arrivals on this route can involve rescue operations, reception needs and possible asylum claims, but an irregular arrival count does not by itself determine a person’s protection status or outcome under Spanish law.

facts.label: Route and destination
facts.value: The Western African Atlantic Route is the sea route from the coasts of West and North Africa to Spain’s Canary Islands; IOM distinguishes it from Spain’s separate Western Mediterranean route.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The Canary Islands are a Spanish Atlantic archipelago close to the West African coast and are an EU outermost region.

facts.label: How arrivals are measured
facts.value: IOM’s Spain flow-monitoring work compiles available daily information on migrants arriving in Spain by sea and land. Arrival figures therefore document recorded entries, rather than the total number of people who departed or attempted the crossing.

facts.label: Risks at sea
facts.value: IOM identifies the Atlantic route as one of the world’s deadliest migration routes, with shipwrecks, boats adrift, and resulting deaths or disappearances among its recurring hazards.

facts.label: Spanish reception and protection context
facts.value: Spain’s humanitarian-assistance program provides emergency coast-response, accommodation, basic health and social support, and transfers for vulnerable migrants who arrive irregularly; people in Spain may separately apply for asylum through authorized channels.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on specific high-volume arrival episodes in the Canary Islands in November 2026, not on all crossings, rescues, asylum decisions, fatalities, or the broader causes and annual trends of migration on the route.
